clue.text: How to get out of a tight situation

definitions.text: How to get out of a tight situation

parts.words: How to get out of a tight situation
parts.note: tight is slang for drunk, so the tight situation is drunkenness, and the way out is regaining sobriety

explanation.surface: Advice on escaping from a tricky predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'tight situation' sounds like a fix or a squeeze; here 'tight' means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering from intoxication is the escape from being tight, that is drunk.

clue.text: Sign of affection

parts.note: affection has an old medical sense, a disease or ailment, so a sign of one is an indication of illness

explanation.surface: A kiss or hug showing fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affection' looks like fondness, but in medicine an affection is a disorder of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical indicator of a disease or disorder, an affection in its clinical sense.

clue.text: Also held by a dandy is a narrow ribbon

indicators.note: one word is held inside another, so the dandy's word holds the other piece

parts.note: a beau is a fashionable man, a dandy
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A fop is wearing a thin strip of ribbon too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dandy' looks like part of the picture but supplies the outer word; 'held by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A headband or thin strip of fabric worn round the hair or as a top is this kind of ribbon.

clue.text: Regret including award for a pleated frilling

indicators.note: the regret word includes, that is contains, the award

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
CH, Companion of Honour, is a British honour or award

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry that a prize came with a frilly trim.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour is a British order, so it serves as the award.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered or pleated strip of fabric used as dress trimming.

clue.text: Men hope an arrangement will result in wonders

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of the preceding words reorders them into new words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Men expect that some plan will produce marvellous results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an arrangement' rearranges MEN HOPE AN; the second 'an' is part of the indicator, the first part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable things or events, marvels, are so called.

clue.text: No way to address a lady

definitions.text: No way to address a lady

parts.words: No way to address a lady
parts.note: the formal letter salutation meant for a man would be the wrong opening when writing to a woman

explanation.surface: A rebuke about speaking rudely to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rudeness; the cryptic reading is that the letter opening suited to a man is wrong for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard formal salutation for a man in a letter is inappropriate for a woman.

clue.text: Bowler out for a duck?

definitions.meaning: Sir Francis ... was famously playing bowls on Plymouth Hoe when the Armada arrived
a male duck is called by this name

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler gets a batsman out without scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, where a 'duck' is a score of nothing; here it is the bird, and the bowler plays bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan seafarer is the most famous game-of-bowls player, and a male mallard bears the same name.

clue.text: One cast by a slanderer

parts.note: slanderers are said to cast slurs on someone's character, the idiom using the verb cast

explanation.surface: Someone chosen for a role by a gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests a role in a play; the idiom is to cast slurs on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A damaging remark or slur, the thing one casts on another's reputation in the idiom.

clue.text: She is trying to make her weighty problem diminish

definitions.text: She is trying to make her weighty problem diminish

parts.words: She is trying to make her weighty problem diminish
parts.note: a dieter wants to reduce her excess weight, the weighty problem

explanation.surface: A woman tackles a serious difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weighty problem' sounds like a serious matter, but it is literal body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A dieter, someone trying to lose weight, is so called.

clue.text: Do exercises again on rough terrain

indicators.note: rough suggests the letters of the next word are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier repeats training drills over uneven ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges TERRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo training a second time, practising skills anew.

clue.text: Spectacular help for Cyclops?

parts.note: spectacular here means relating to spectacles; a one-eyed giant would need a single lens

explanation.surface: An impressive aid for the one-eyed giant of myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacular' means to do with spectacles, not impressive; the Cyclops has only one eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A single eyeglass suits a creature with one eye.

clue.text: Fix with a soft tip

parts.note: P is piano, the musical abbreviation for soft
a point is a sharp tip

explanation.surface: Repair something using a gentle tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a date or time is to name or set it; also to assign someone to a post.

clue.text: For that reason the judge has some Scandinavian money

parts.note: a referee, ref, judges a game
the ore is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: A judge owns some Nordic currency, hence the conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The ore is a hundredth of a krona or krone.
explanation.definitionFit: A connective meaning consequently, hence.

clue.text: Rugby doctor having a dance

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A rugby medic takes to the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Shape of growth on old food

definitions.meaning: to form or fashion something, or a cast for forming it
the furry fungus that forms on stale bread or cheese

explanation.surface: The look of the furry patch on stale leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A form or template for shaping, and a fungal coating on decaying food.

clue.text: Discredit engineers in the argument

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, the engineers inside the argument

parts.note: a dispute is an argument
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers discredit each other during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers is a British army corps, a regular crossword source of RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of good name, disgrace; a noun matching the noun sense of the definition.

clue.text: Nobleman, that is to say Ronald previously

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is to say
Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: A peer, namely Ronald, from before.
explanation.definitionFit: At an earlier time, before now.

clue.text: Fetching animal

parts.note: fetching means attractive, but here it is a creature that fetches, bringing back game

explanation.surface: A good-looking creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' looks like 'attractive'; read it as 'that fetches'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog bred to bring back shot game.

clue.text: Repeated various instances

indicators.note: various, meaning diverse, signals the letters of the next word take a different order

explanation.surface: Many different examples recur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges INSTANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Continual, unceasing, going on again and again.

clue.text: Visible perception

definitions.meaning: able to be seen, within view, read as two words

explanation.surface: Perception of what can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means within view; whole, it means deep understanding.

clue.text: Football club on the south coast without a win

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Football club on the south coast without a win', gives no parse for CHELSEA, a London club; the text appears garbled and no source gives the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: Football club on the south coast without a win

clue.text: Well-known having made a record

explanation.surface: Someone became famous after cutting a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous, distinguished; and also past tense of jotting down.

clue.text: Defame a large number in sus- R pension of hostilities

indicators.note: the pieces go in the suspension of hostilities

parts.note: a truce suspends fighting
D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number

explanation.surface: Slandering many people during a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and D (500 in Roman numerals) inside TRUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce is to slander or malign someone.

clue.text: Girl with theologian went in front despite having been dis, honest

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Girl with theologian went in front despite having been dis, honest', is garbled: DI + DD + LED gives the letters but 'despite' and 'dis, honest' leave no sound definition.
annotationWithheld.clue: Girl with theologian went in front despite having been dis, honest

clue.text: Noisy outburst on stage

definitions.meaning: a public display of temper, as in making a fuss
a theatrical setting, a division of a play

explanation.surface: Someone throws a tantrum on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public fuss, and a division or setting of a play.

clue.text: Cause of that sinking feeling on the beach?

definitions.text: Cause of that sinking feeling on the beach?

parts.words: Cause of that sinking feeling on the beach?
parts.note: a sinking feeling usually means dread, but here someone is literally sinking into wet sand

explanation.surface: What makes a beachgoer feel dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that sinking feeling' is the idiom for dismay; here the sinking is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose waterlogged sand that swallows anyone standing on it.

clue.text: Doubt how much in France is on therailway

parts.note: que is French for how or how much in exclamations
printed run together for 'the railway'; RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Uncertainty over French fares on the trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A question or uncertainty raised about something.

clue.text: Unusually stark limestone formation

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the next word arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A strangely bleak rocky landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges STARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape of eroded limestone with sinkholes and caves.

clue.text: One of th actions that speak louder than words?

definitions.text: One of th actions that speak louder than words

parts.words: One of th actions that speak louder than words
parts.note: the proverb says actions speak louder than words; a body movement conveys meaning silently

explanation.surface: A nod to the proverb about deeds over talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is taken literally: a movement of the hand says something without words.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement of hand or head expressing meaning, communication without speech.

clue.text: In effect having been chaste

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'In effect having been chaste', gives VIRTUAL for 'In effect' but 'having been chaste' has no sound parse or second definition found.

clue.text: Attempt to include old people in play

indicators.note: the attempt is made to include, so to contain, the old people

parts.note: a try is an attempt
the aged are elderly people

explanation.surface: Trying to cast elderly actors in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old people' is a plural noun phrase, matching the aged as a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious drama ending in disaster for its hero.

clue.text: Again step on a tyre

definitions.meaning: to tread on a second time
a used tyre given a new tread

explanation.surface: Stepping once more on a car's wheel cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk over again; and a remoulded tyre with fresh grooves.
